subject.title: [Bug]: OpenClaw Tool Lifecycle / Gateway Recovery Field Report

question: Should successful tool execution followed by failed assistant continuation be recovered through session-survival/quarantine semantics, durable lifecycle receipts, or a narrower replay policy for selected safe cases?
rationale: Current code deliberately fails closed after possible side effects, while the issue asks for deterministic recovery; choosing what can safely resume, retry, or be quarantined is a product and safety decision before implementation.

options.title: Session-survival and quarantine first
options.body: Define durable liveness/quarantine semantics so replay-unsafe incomplete turns cannot poison future context and users get a clear resume or reset path.

options.title: Receipt-only observability
options.body: Add richer tool lifecycle receipts and diagnostics without changing retry or session-recovery behavior, improving manual recovery but not automatic continuation.

options.title: Narrow safe replay policy
options.body: Allow retries only for provably idempotent or no-side-effect current-turn states while preserving fail-closed behavior for unknown tools and committed side effects.

recommendation.title: Session-survival and quarantine first
recommendation.body: Define durable liveness/quarantine semantics so replay-unsafe incomplete turns cannot poison future context and users get a clear resume or reset path.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the current terminal-classifier and replay-safety implementation and recent merged recovery work in the affected files.
